ThingDef.label: Type 86 WTC2
ThingDef.description:
Caliber: 5.8x42mm. 30-round detachable mag. Select-Fire.
The Type 86 WTC1 is an experimental Chinese bullpup rifle developed in the 1980s. Despite the recent adoption of the Type 81 assault rifle, the PLA continued to invest in programs to develop new small arms weaponry, taking a keen interest in a few recent external trends - the rise in the adoption of bullpup firearms (such as the Austrian Steyr AUG, French FAMAS, and British SA80), and the ongoing switch to lighter cartridges (as western states moved from .308 battle rifles to 5.56mm assault rifles, and the USSR adopted the 5.45x39mm AK-74 to replace the AKM.) The WTC1 and WTC2 rifles were products of this development, although neither was ever put into service. However, the design specs of the WTC rifles were used to help develop the civilian export Type 86S rifle, and China would eventually adopt a bullpup rifle in the QBZ-95 a decade later.
The WTC2 variant was developed to test the 5.8x42mm round that was also being developed at the time.
